verdict.rationale: Homebrew is a CLI with documented headless and CI use. Installation supports `NONINTERACTIVE=1`, and the `.pkg` installer handles unattended MDM installs. The manpage directs certain commands to administrative scripts and scheduled jobs, including when no user is logged in, and shows `--yes` usage. Brew Bundle docs say one command sets up dependencies in CI services such as GitHub Actions and give the scriptable `brew bundle check || brew bundle install` idiom. One community comment calls Homebrew brittle on CI, but it cites no specific failure, so it lowers confidence rather than creating a dispute. Missing for 10: a dedicated CI/automation guide or official CI action in evidence, and independent hands-on corroboration of reliable CI operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.
You can use this behaviour in scripts like so: brew bundle check || brew bundle install
Use this in administrative scripts and scheduled jobs to manage an existing installation, including when no user is logged in.
If you're on macOS, try our `.pkg` installer for interactive or unattended MDM installs.
